Summary: The AlphaFold protein structure prediction system was developed by DeepMind, a company that is a subsidiary of Alphabet. The system was created to predict a protein’s 3D structure from its amino acid sequence, and it has achieved accuracy competitive with experimental methods. DeepMind partnered with EMBL’s European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI) to create AlphaFold DB, which makes these predictions freely available to the scientific community.

Summary: The AlphaFold paper developers are Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of DeepMind, a subsidiary of Alphabet. The sources confirm that DeepMind made the AlphaFold code publicly available in 2021 and that Demis Hassabis cofounded DeepMind and is one of the leaders of the AlphaFold project. The sources also mention that Jumper was part of the DeepMind team that participated in CASP13 in 2018 and now leads the DeepMind structure prediction group.
